utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence doesn't have any particular matter to raise. At the previous Status Conference, you set a deadline when the Prosecution should disclose all the material under the Rules and file the pre-trial brief. The Defence was asked to say how much time it would need for its brief. As for the tempo of disclosure, I feel that we still haven't received sufficient material to be able to indicate how much time the Defence will need to process all this and to file its own brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So you are not in the position to say how much time to prepare once you receive the pre-trial brief from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I had any indication of the volume of documents; I must point out that the indictment covers a five-year period. It includes Bosnia-Herzegovina and Croatia. So I expect quite a lot of material. Mr. Groome suggested to disclose revised or edited witness statements. I said that I would be grateful to Mr. Groome if he gives me any material that he has. And I will consider the disclosure to be completed once I have all the relevant information. Mr. Groome said that this will involve certain delays. He will probably tell you about that. I think all the transcripts under 66(A) have not been translated. So there are quite a number of things that the Prosecution has still not done. And if we were to see the end of this process, then the Defence would be able to take a position about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll come to the issue after all the disclosure is completed and the pre-trial brief from the Prosecution is filed. Now I will turn to Mr. Groome, then. How are the cases going on the part of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have prepared an oral report. If it please the Court, I'll give the Court my report on the state of the disclosure for both Rule 66 and 68, as well as --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: -- to the other issues. As an overview of disclosure, as approved by the Court in the last Status Conference, the Prosecution has been meeting its disclosure obligation by making monthly instalments of both Rule 68 and Rule 66 material. So far to date the Prosecution has disclosed a total of 65 compact disks containing both Rule ^23 68 material and Rule 66 material. The Rule 68 material is in fully searchable format so that both Defence counsel are able to search through those documents for material that they believe may be relevant for their defence. We are on track to complete our disclosure requirement of both 66(A)(2) and Rule 68 by the 19th of July this year. And that disclosure will be complete with respect to translations as well. With respect to the current status of 66 A (ii), to date the Prosecution has disclosed 86 statements of witnesses that it intends to call. Most of those are the primary statement that was taken by the Office of the Prosecutor. We are still, however, in the process of conducting all of the searches required to identify any other material that may be discoverable under that same Rule, and we are still in the process of getting all of those statements translated so that we can meet, fully meet our obligation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Pausing there. What do you mean by primary statement? The Prosecution is planning to make another statement, revised form, and disclose it at a later stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. What I mean by that is what we've been able to locate now and disclose now are the primary statements taken by the Office of the Prosecutor. We are currently searching our document database to identify are there other notes or are there other materials which would be discloseable under Rule 66 (A)(ii).

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Later this week we will be disclosing 16 redacted documents, and these are the documents that Mr. Jovanovic referred to. The Prosecution will be filing an application seeking delayed disclosure for some of the witnesses that have particular security concerns. In order to facilitate the Defence completing their preparation, I have agreed to, in advance of filing that application or the Chamber ruling on it, providing copies of the statements with the identifying information redacted. Once the Chamber makes a ruling on what protective measures are appropriate for each of those witnesses, I will then take whatever steps are necessary to fully comply with the Chamber's order. I expect that that will be that some statements will have to be provided in fully unredacted form, and I expect that perhaps some of those applications will be granted and we will be allowed to delay disclosure of identifying information to a later period of time. With respect to Rule 68, to date, 30.308 documents have been disclosed, again, in a searchable format, so that both Defence counsel can search those documents using a Word text to identify any material that they feel may be relevant to their particular defence. These are documents that staff of the Office of the Prosecutor have identified through computer searches and have reviewed and have determined may be material that's covered under Rule 68. We had offered earlier on in the case to include with our computer searches any terms or phrases that both Defence counsel would like us to search for in order to pull out additional documents. I would just inform them here at this Status Conference that from the end of this week, unless we receive those terms it may not be possible to complete those searches and to complete that disclosure by July 19th. We will, of course, always accommodate them and search our records for the terms that they request us to search our records for, and that will be disclosed to them as soon as possible. With respect to expert reports, Your Honour, the Prosecution will -- we are already having an expert look at some of the documents in this case. I anticipate by the end of this month, a primary portion of that report will be able to be disclosed. The second part of that report, a supplement to that report, may be a month later. It may even be the 19th of July before we can disclose that final report. The last expert's work will build upon the analytical work of this expert I've just been referring to. It is my hope that he will have completed his work as well, but if not, what I would be tendering or providing on the 19th of July would be that expert report in its most current state. And of course I will do everything I can to try to expedite the final completion of that report. Now, with respect to taking or offering evidence in written form under Rule 92 bis, we are still in the process of reviewing those witnesses to see if such treatment of that evidence is appropriate. As a principle, we will be using 92 bis wherever we believe it is legally appropriate and we hope to file a motion with respect to that in the fall. I'd like to say a few things about that. To date, 49 witnesses have been identified as being appropriate for treatment under 92 bis (A), some of those -- with cross-examination, we would make the argument that cross-examination is not required. I have the breakdown here, if the Court wishes me to go into how many of 92 bis (A), (C), and (D). Your Honour, what I would propose is when the Prosecution makes its 65 ter filing on the 19th of July, I would ask my colleagues at the Defence bar to review what we have identified as witnesses that can be taken under 92 bis. I would ask that when we resume in the fall, that if they could identify to the Prosecution which, if any, of those witnesses they would consent to be taken as 92 bis. Obviously, it is still for the Court to make the final determination, but at least in our application to the Court for the 92 bis we would be able to inform the Chamber which witnesses have been agreed to and which witnesses are being contested. With respect to adjudicated facts: We have had our first meeting. All parties undertook certain commitments to do some additional work and have additional discussions with their respective clients. We will meet sometime later this week and continue our discussions with respect to that. With respect to the pre-trial brief, Your Honour, it is still our intention to file that as per the Court's order. It is my intention, unless the Court would direct otherwise, to also file the following: As an appendix to that pre-trial brief, a list of facts from the CaseMap programme. The case should be fully CaseMapped by that stage and it is our intention to list for the benefit of the Defence counsel and for the Court a list of all the facts that we intend to introduce proof of at trial. In addition to that, an appendix of what we would call the Prosecution's trial plan, it will contain all of the information we are required to provide the Court pursuant to Rule 65 ter, plus some additional details, so that the Chamber can see precisely the case in the exact form that we intend to prove it. I'm available, Your Honour. That's all I have. I'm available to answer any questions by the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Having heard that, I would very much encourage the Prosecution to meet the deadline, at least, and to expedite the procedure, so complete its disclosure well before the deadline. But that -- we'll see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If there's any comment from Mr. Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then that concludes our Status Conference for Mr. Simatovic.
